column2: Long counted as the heaviest stable isotope, until 2003, when it was caught decaying. Its half-life is about a billion times the age of the universe, which makes it a favourite fact.
The heaviest nucleus ever made: 118 protons and 176 neutrons. Only a handful of atoms have ever existed, each lasting under a millisecond.
